coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02/K06 as a product, but timing evidence changed. Labour Ministry spokesman (Al Mamlaka/Al Jazeera, June 2026): the status-regularisation window for irregular foreign workers, households included, closed 30 Sep 2026 with no extension. From 1 Oct 2026 a 'deportation' flag goes on irregular workers, and ministry urged home owners to regularise. About 64k permits issued/renewed since June. EY tax news (15 Jun 2026) reports MoL suspended foreign-worker recruitment from 1 Jun 2026 with unspecified exceptions; I could not confirm whether domestic workers are exempt. Recruitment-office licensing resumed under Regulation 63/2020 after a 12-year freeze (Al Mamlaka 142945). Households alone are a poor buyer group, so a household tracker is a variant of K02.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No Jordanian licensing or purchase-register rule found in Arabic or English. Jordan News (2021) says licensed scrap shops exist but gives no rules, regulator or record duty, and notes many dealers work from vehicles without a permit. Marked unverified; the regulator and any buyer-ID register rule are unchecked.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Jordanian second-hand dealer or pawnbroker regime surfaced. Pawnbroking is likely not a licensed activity here (unverified). Used-car showrooms: no specific instructions found. Tourist car-rental offices must keep records of renters' names, nationalities and addresses (1984 Traffic Law regulation, a licence also under the 2009 regulation); see candidate.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05. New AML/CFT instructions for jewellery shops published in the Official Gazette (Al Mamlaka 153485, article Oct-Nov 2024): judicial bail for new shops raised from 5,000 to 10,000 JD; sanctions escalate to closure up to 2 weeks, bail forfeiture or licence cancellation. The article does not mention a register, reporting or goAML.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Jordanian dismantler or scrap-vehicle rule found. Results were Saudi only. Unverified; the regulator (LTRC, Traffic department, Ministry of Environment or municipality) is unchecked.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K16. Greater Amman Municipality runs electronic registration for Eid al-Adha sacrificial-animal stalls (Jordan News, 2025); this is seasonal and municipal. Poultry slaughterhouse licensing is under Directive Z/16 of 2003.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Greater Amman Municipality issued Slaughterhouse Regulation and Monitoring Regulation No. 84 of 2024, replacing No. 145 of 2016 (FAOLEX/LEAP summary; full page returned 403 on fetch). GAM slaughterhouse director says vets join unified inspection teams, and consumers are told to look for the official slaughterhouse stamp. No butcher-side record or reporting duty confirmed.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Budget used on higher-yield categories; no search run.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary drugs are regulated by the Ministry of Agriculture under the 2022-amended instructions for veterinary drugs, biologics and pesticides (Agriculture Law 13/2015); the ACI-hosted PDF was not opened. A Eremnews investigation reports unregistered 'fake vets' running vet pharmacies in Amman against the Veterinary Association registry. No buyer-side duty (dispensing register, prescription log) confirmed.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Water Authority Service Guide 2025-2026 (mwi.gov.jo) lists a wells and drilling services section, but the snippet did not show duties. No drilling-licence or abstraction-reporting rule confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Nothing Jordan-specific. Only fact: some wastewater plants are designated to receive tanker (sewage-truck) loads; no tracking or licence rule found. Saudi 'Tasreeh' tanker-tracking platform is a foreign analogue only.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Jordanian lift, boiler or pressure-vessel inspection rule found in two searches; results were UAE, Israel, Saudi and TUV pages. Unverified; Ministry of Labour OSH regulations and the JSMO accreditation list (opendata.gov.jo) are a start point.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search run; budget.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pesticides are governed by Instructions G/7 of 2021 (86 articles under Agriculture Law 13/2015; retail only of Ministry-registered products). Directive Z/47 of 2003 licenses pesticide shops and spraying-service offices through the Plant Protection Department (FAOLEX). No 2025 amendment found and no sales-register duty confirmed.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K06. Domestic-worker offices are licensed under Regulation 63/2020 (older rules: partnership company, 50k JD capital, bank guarantee 75k JD, annual renewal and classification; the older text is not confirmed current). Recruitment suspension from 1 Jun 2026 could cut the case volume K06 depends on; scope unverified. The draft Labour Law also sets conditions for employment/placement companies (Parlmany, Jul 2026, unread).

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No Jordanian cemetery or funeral-service rule found; results were foreign. Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations Registry (Ministry of Social Development) has an online platform, 'Takamul', launched mid-2023, per an ARDD/Jonaf June 2024 report; the PDF text could not be read. ICNL describes a fragmented legal framework. Reporting deadlines were not confirmed. Halal supervision not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Land Transport Regulatory Commission launched phase 1 on 17 Jun 2026 of 17 e-services (permit renewals for service, regular, airport, hotel and tourist taxis, buses, school transport, limousines, office rental vehicles, plus company licences) at eservices.ltrc.gov.jo; 47 services by end-2026, and 100 (50 passenger, 50 freight) planned. Logins are issued in person at governorate offices. This is a free state portal, so it competes with any renewal tracker. Fleet: 990 service taxis, 5,202 public vehicles, 683 large buses, 3,529 medium buses.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: nothing new beyond K17. Street vendors: Regulation on Peddlers, Stalls, Canopies and Kiosks applies to all municipalities except Greater Amman. No e-licensing found. Vendors are low-value and informal.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries: nothing new beyond K07. Driving-training centres are under Regulation No. 102 of 2008 (instructor needs Category 4 licence for 2 years, JD 500 bank guarantee renewed annually); no newer rule found. Home-based food: Airbnb help page says JFDA and GAM license home meal service, renewed annually (third-party, unverified). Tattoo and hunting not searched.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Licensing sits with the Energy and Minerals Regulatory Commission (EMRC). 9 station/LPG-agency applications refused (undated); a 2024 draft amendment to the petroleum-derivatives licensing system sets fees; CNG vehicle stations are being approved. No small-operator recurring filing found beyond licensing, and the sector has established station-management vendors (not checked). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Grain is state-run: the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply (MIT) runs wheat/barley tenders and the General Silos and Supply Co. handles intake, with farmer origin certificates from the Ministry of Agriculture (3,100 issued). No mill or feed-store licensing instructions surfaced. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: The Jordan Cooperative Corporation publishes registry statistics on opendata.gov.jo (dataset 'statistics of cooperative societies numbers 554'; counts not visible on the page I fetched). Regulation and audit instructions not found. Candidate left unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: The TPA claims idea is already K01. New unverified lead: radiation-source licences for dental and X-ray clinics. A jordanianlaw.com page defines facility, practice and personal radiation licences, but I could not confirm the regulator's current renewal rules.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pharmacies keep a daily prescription log for controlled drugs, under a JFDA decision of 1 Feb 2017. Secure prescription forms are in use under Narcotics Law 23 of 2016. JFDA was studying an electronic import-to-patient tracking project in Jan 2024, and I found no evidence it has launched. No pharmacy-specific compliance software surfaced.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: No Jordan-specific rules for security-company licensing or labour-supply companies surfaced; searches returned other countries. The migrant-worker permit side is already K02 and K06, and MoL publishes a work-permit guide (Nov 2025 and 21 Jan 2026 editions). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: The Contractors Association law requires licensing then classification. EMRC closed 82 non-compliant quarries in Q1 2018. No current classification instructions, renewal rules or recurring filings found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: The search returned only UAE goAML material; Jordan's AML supervisor for real-estate brokers could not be confirmed. Professional billing is K04 and gold dealers are K05. Insurance agents and brokers are now supervised by the CBJ under Insurance Business Regulation Law 12 of 2021 (per a secondary source); candidate 35.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guest houses (بيوت الضيافة) run under the 2019 Organisational Instructions: a guest register with an ID copy shown to security on arrival, annual licence 1 Jan to 31 Dec, one site per host, sales tax filing, and a mandatory Jordan Hotels Association membership. Hotel apartments need a classification certificate, and the annual renewal needs a civil-liability policy. No Jordan short-term-rental (Airbnb) regime found. No Jordan-specific guest-register software found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: JFDA issues export health certificates, with a JFDA office inside the Amman Chamber of Industry. The Agricultural Marketing Office sets export standards. Nothing specific to small exporters, and the export portals are state-run. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 31. Care centres for people with disabilities and the elderly (Ministry of Social Development)
coverage.found: Disability Centres Regulation 2014: annual licence renewal, annual financial and administrative report to the ministry, administrative/financial/technical records, mandatory electronic surveillance equipment. Early-intervention centres have separate 2017 regulation and 2019 licensing instructions. In Nov 2025 the ministry announced quality standards for rehabilitation centres. Elderly-home rules not located.

coverage.category: 32. Tourist vehicle rental offices (Land Transport Regulatory Commission)
coverage.found: The amended licensing system (2026, per Al Mamlaka/Motory) raises minimum capital and the bank guarantee to JD 15,000. The union head estimates 60 percent of offices could close (unverified, partisan). The duty is a licensing barrier, not a recurring filing.

coverage.category: 33. Municipal business-licence renewal and e-licensing
coverage.found: Petra, 21 Apr 2026: the Cabinet extended the penalty-free business-licence renewal period in municipal areas to 30 June (2026), and owners must complete e-licensing. Deadline has passed; later extensions not checked.

coverage.category: 34. Vocational and technical training providers (Professional Work law)
coverage.found: On 25 Jan 2026 the Cabinet approved the justifications for a draft Professional Work Regulation Law 2026, requiring vocational and technical training companies and institutions to hold Ministry of Labour licences. This is still a draft, and I found no final text.

coverage.category: 35. Insurance agents and brokers (CBJ-supervised)
coverage.found: The regulator appears to be the Central Bank of Jordan under Insurance Business Regulation Law 12 of 2021 (secondary source). Licensing and reporting rules for small agents not found.

coverage.category: 36. Hosts and landlords of foreign visitors: Oct 2025 residence-registration rule
coverage.found: A Mexican embassy notice says amendments to the 1973 Residence and Foreigners Law apply from Oct 2025: certain-visa foreigners must register their address at the police within 14 days (JD 200 fine). The duty falls on the guest, not the host. Unverified, from a secondary source.
